newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fini says confidence motion "shameless".
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fini says confidence motion "shameless".

text.p: Gianfranco Fini, leader of Italy's hard-right National Alliance party, on Wednesday denounced the government's use of a confidence vote to push through development projects as a "shameless" tactic.
"The climate has worsened since yesterday because what they have done with Bagnoli is shameless," Fini told reporters.
The government will begin voting at 1500 GMT on a decree whose main thrust is the Bagnoli project near the southern port city of Naples.
The government wants to turn a former steel works into a huge park surrounded by hotels, restaurants, beaches, a tourist marina and quality housing.

The decree would also release funds for the development of rundown industrial areas in the northern city of Milan as set out in a cabinet bill due to expire on November 20. The bill has been dogged for months by filibustering from opposition parties.

A recent ruling by the Constitutional Court means that Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government can no longer routinely re-issue expiring draft government laws. They must now be approved by parliament or dropped.

The centre-right Freedom Alliance wants the region of Campania and the province of Naples, which it controls, also to have a say in the Bagnoli redevelopment, rather than just the city hall which is controlled by the centre-left.
Freedom Alliance party leaders in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) later met Chamber speaker Luciano Violante to protest against the timetable for debate on the 1997 budget.
The budget was due to have come before the chamber on Thursday but has now been rescheduled for Friday. The house will discuss other expiring decrees on Thursday instead.
